candidates.description: Made from fermented Korean red chili paste (gochujang), it is balanced with toasted sesame oil, garlic, sweeteners (sugar or honey), and soy sauce. This essential mixture brings umami-rich heat to rice bowls, often featuring a glossy, slightly runny consistency. BASE SAUCE – Gochujang–Sesame–Vinegar (Weights for 50)
methodSteps: Whisk gochujang, soy, vinegar and honey until smooth. Stir in garlic, ginger, sesame oil and water to a thick-pour consistency. Fold through sesame seeds and spring onion. Rest 30 minutes before use.
This can be cooked for a finishing sauce/glaze can also be thickened with a cornflour slurry
It has a consistency that is designed to be easily mixed into a bowl of rice and various toppings, often smoother and more pourable than the thick gochujang paste

candidates.description: BASE GLAZE – Gochujang–Doenjang BBQ (Weights for 50) "BBQ House Style" Ssamjang Soy-Chilli Glaze is a savory, nutty, and slightly spicy paste designed to mimic the authentic dipping sauces served at Korean BBQ restaurants. It is primarily used for spreading on lettuce wraps (ssam) with grilled meat, but it also works as a thick glaze for meats or vegetables.
methodSteps: Whisk gochujang + doenjang smooth with soy and water. Add honey, sugar, vinegar, garlic, ginger. Simmer 10 mins. Cool slightly and stir in sesame oil, sesame seeds, spring onion. Brush/glaze proteins.
BBQ House Style Enhancements
Onion: Add 500g finely chopped white onion for extra crunch or lightly pickled red onion with the spring onion as garnish
Green Chili: Add one finely chopped green chili (like a Korean green pepper or jalapeno) for more heat.
Sake/Mirin: Add 1 tbsp of mirin (sweet rice wine) for a more restaurant-style savory depth.

It is characterized by using generous amounts of kimchi brine and water (or anchovy stock) for a 20-minute, one-pot, umami-rich stew. BASE BROTH – Kimchi–Chilli–Garlic (Weights for 50)
methodSteps: Sweat onion in sesame oil. Add garlic/ginger. Add kimchi and cook 10–15 minutes until fragrant. Add gochugaru + gochujang, cook out. Add stock, radish, soy, sugar. Simmer 45–60 mins. Finish with spring onion.

paragraphs: 3) KIMCHI & GOCHUGARU STEW BASE (Kimchi-jjigae Style – Busan)

This Busan-style Kimchi-jjigae base focuses on rendering fatty pork belly and frying aged kimchi with gochugaru (Korean red pepper flakes) and gochujang (red pepper paste) to build a deeply Savory, spicy broth. It is characterized by using generous amounts of kimchi brine and water (or anchovy stock) for a 20-minute, one-pot, umami-rich stew.

Sweat onion in sesame oil. Add garlic/ginger. Add kimchi and cook 10–15 minutes until fragrant. Add gochugaru + gochujang, cook out. Add stock, radish, soy, sugar. Simmer 45–60 mins. Finish with spring onion.
Add tofu and simmer for 3–4 minutes. Top with green onions and a drizzle of sesame oil.

candidates.description: A Gochujang Sticky Glaze (Korean Fried Style) is a thick, syrupy, and vibrant red sauce that balances, sweet, Savory, and spicy Flavors. Primarily used for coating crispy fried chicken (yangnyeom), it provides a "funk" and umami depth due to the fermented pepper paste. BASE GLAZE – Sweet–Spicy Sticky (Weights for 50)
methodSteps: Simmer all ingredients (except sesame oil) for 10–15 minutes. If needed, thicken lightly with slurry. Remove from heat and stir in sesame oil. Toss fried items in glaze to coat.
Adjust Heat: If too spicy, add more sugar or honey.
Consistency: The sauce should be "thick and syrupy" when done, usually taking only a few minutes to reduce.
Garlic Intensity: Using grated, rather than minced, garlic helps it infuse better without burning.

The broth is usually simmered with dried anchovies, kelp (dashi), radish, and sometimes onion, then strained and cooked with soft tofu and seafood. candidates.description: This Savory braising sauce, based on a mixture of toasted almonds, onions, and the North African spice blend Ras el Hanout, is often paired with poultry or eggs, creating a rich, textured sauce that is both nutty and deeply aromatic. The base acts as a thickener and flavouring agent, commonly used in Moroccan-style tagines or stews. BASE SAUCE – Almond–Onion–Ras el Hanout (Weights for 50) Roughly chopped hard-boiled eggs are commonly stirred in at the end for added creaminess, or raw eggs can be cracked into the sauce and poached in the final minutes of cooking.
methodSteps: Caramelise onions deeply (this is key). Add garlic and spices. Add stock. Blend almonds with hot stock to a smooth almond cream, stir into sauce. Simmer 20 mins. Temper eggs into sauce (whisk eggs with hot sauce then return) and cook gently to thicken. Do not boil hard.

Add coconut cream: Simmer until glossy and slightly reduced.
Build sauce: Add coconut milk + stock. Simmer 20–25 mins.
Season: Palm sugar → fish sauce → soy. Balance sweet/salt.
Finish: Add lime juice, basil, kaffir lime leaves last.

candidates.description: Laab (or Larb) is a vibrant, spicy, and sour minced meat salad from Northeastern Thailand (Isaan) and Laos, traditionally featuring pork, chicken, or beef mixed with lime juice, fish sauce, chili flakes, and toasted rice powder. Key components include fresh herbs like mint, coriander, and shallots, served with sticky rice. BASE SAUCE – Larb Dressing Essential Ingredient: Khao khua (toasted sticky rice powder) provides a nutty flavour and thickens the dressing. Toast uncooked glutinous rice in a dry pan until golden brown and fragrant, then grind into a coarse powder.
methodSteps: Dissolve sugar into lime + fish sauce.
Add chilli flakes.
Toss cooked mince with dressing while warm.
Add roasted rice powder last.
Fold through herbs just before service.

candidates.description: Tom Yum Goong (Bangkok Style) is an iconic Thai hot and sour broth-based soup, celebrated for its complex, aromatic, and fiery flavor profile. The Bangkok-style broth is renowned for its intense, immediate infusion of fresh herbs, offering a clear (Nam Sai) or slightly creamy (Nam Khon) texture. BASE SAUCE – Tom Yum Broth (Aromatic) The base is defined by the "Tom Yum Trinity"—lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves—which create an intensely fragrant, earthy, and citrusy aroma. Aromatics: Lemongrass (bruised), Galangal (sliced), Kaffir Lime Leaves (torn), Shallots, and Bird’s Eye Chilies. Flavor Profiles: A balance of hot (chilies), sour (lime), savory/umami (fish sauce), and a touch of sweetness (sugar). Key Ingredient: Nam Prik Pao (roasted chili paste) is essential, adding a mild smoky, savory-sweet depth to the broth.
methodSteps: Bring stock to simmer. Add lemongrass, galangal, kaffir, chillies, garlic, coriander stems.
Simmer 25 mins (do not boil hard).
Add mushrooms + tomatoes, simmer 5–6 mins.
Season with fish sauce + palm sugar.
Turn heat off. Add lime juice last.
Optional: whisk in evaporated milk for creamy version.

paragraphs: 2) TOM YUM GOONG – HOT & SOUR BROTH (Bangkok)

Tom Yum Goong (Bangkok Style) is an iconic Thai hot and sour broth-based soup, celebrated for its complex, aromatic, and fiery flavor profile. The Bangkok-style broth is renowned for its intense, immediate infusion of fresh herbs, offering a clear (Nam Sai) or slightly creamy (Nam Khon) texture.
The base is defined by the "Tom Yum Trinity"—lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves—which create an intensely fragrant, earthy, and citrusy aroma.
Aromatics: Lemongrass (bruised), Galangal (sliced), Kaffir Lime Leaves (torn), Shallots, and Bird’s Eye Chilies.
Flavor Profiles: A balance of hot (chilies), sour (lime), savory/umami (fish sauce), and a touch of sweetness (sugar).
Key Ingredient: Nam Prik Pao (roasted chili paste) is essential, adding a mild smoky, savory-sweet depth to the broth.
Bring stock to simmer. Add lemongrass, galangal, kaffir, chillies, garlic, coriander stems.
Season with fish sauce + palm sugar.
Turn heat off. Add lime juice last.
Optional: whisk in evaporated milk for creamy version.
Finishing Touches: A large amount of fresh lime juice (added after heat is turned off to avoid bitterness), fish sauce, and fresh coriander

Base Sauce Components (Ingredients)The authentic Bangkok-style sauce is characterized by a "sauce trio" (or quartet) that brings the umami, commonly including: Fish Sauce: Provides deep, authentic saltiness. Dark Soy Sauce: Used sparingly for a rich, caramel-like colour (often omitted in "purest" versions, but standard in Bangkok street style).

candidates.description: Khao Soi is a renowned Northern Thai (Chiang Mai) curry noodle soup, characterized by a rich, creamy, and mildly spicy golden broth made from a coconut milk base. This broth base is typically a blended paste that creates a thick, velvety "gravy" rather than a thin soup. BASE SAUCE – Khao Soi Curry Broth

ingredients.name: Khao soi paste
ingredients.rawText: Khao soi paste: 2.0–2.4kg(or red curry paste 1.6–2.0kg + curry powder 80g + turmeric 35g)

methodSteps: Fry paste in oil 5–6 mins (add curry powder + turmeric if using red paste).
Add coconut cream, simmer 5 mins.
Add coconut milk + stock. Simmer 25 mins.
Season with fish sauce, sugar, tamarind.
Finish with lime juice last.

Traditional Serving Style:The completed curry broth is poured over boiled egg noodles and topped with a generous amount of crispy, deep-fried egg noodles. It is served with condiments like pickled mustard greens, raw shallots, lime wedges, and chili oil.

Khao Soi is a renowned Northern Thai (Chiang Mai) curry noodle soup, characterized by a rich, creamy, and mildly spicy golden broth made from a coconut milk base. This broth base is typically a blended paste that creates a thick, velvety "gravy" rather than a thin soup.
BASE SAUCE – Khao Soi Curry Broth
Khao soi paste: 2.0–2.4kg(or red curry paste 1.6–2.0kg + curry powder 80g + turmeric 35g)
Fry paste in oil 5–6 mins (add curry powder + turmeric if using red paste).
Add coconut milk + stock. Simmer 25 mins.
Season with fish sauce, sugar, tamarind.

Traditional Serving Style:The completed curry broth is poured over boiled egg noodles and topped with a generous amount of crispy, deep-fried egg noodles. It is served with condiments like pickled mustard greens, raw shallots, lime wedges, and chili oil.
Crispy fried noodles, pickled mustard greens, red onion, chilli oil, lime wedge

candidates.description: This recipe for Tuscan Porcini & Polenta Bowls features creamy, slow-cooked polenta topped with a rich, savoury mushroom ragu made with Marsala wine and cream. Inspired by rustic Italian Flavors, this dish is designed to be served in bowls, offering a luxurious, Savory experience. BASE SAUCE: Mushroom & Marsala Cream (50 portions)
methodSteps: Soak dried porcini in hot stock 30 mins, strain and keep liquid.
Sweat shallots in butter + oil 10 mins.
Add garlic, then mushrooms, cook hard to drive off water.
Add marsala, reduce by half.
Add porcini liquid, simmer 15 mins.
Add cream, simmer 10 mins.
Finish with parmesan, parsley, lemon.

candidates.description: Ribollita is a classic, hearty Tuscan bread and vegetable soup, traditionally hailing from the Florence region, known as a "cucina povera" (peasant cooking) dish designed to use up leftovers. The name translates to "reboiled," as it is typically made by simmering day-old bread with bean and vegetable broth, often being reheated over several days for better flavour. BASE SAUCE: Tomato & Kale Broth with Olive Oil (50 portions) While traditionally vegetarian, some versions may include pancetta or be made with meat broth. Other variations include adding white wine to the soffritto for acidity or using kale, swiss chard, or spinach interchangeably based on seasonality.

candidates.description: Siena Pici Pasta Bowls feature thick, hand-rolled Tuscan pasta tossed in a rich base sauce of nutty browned butter, fragrant sage, and sharp Pecorino Romano cheese. This rustic, Savory dish is often finished with black pepper, providing a simple yet flavourful coating for the chewy pasta. BASE SAUCE: Garlic & Sage Butter with Pecorino (50 portions) Base Sauce (Garlic & Sage Butter): Fresh sage leaves are sizzled in butter until fragrant and slightly browned (burnt butter or burro nocciola).
methodSteps: Melt butter + olive oil gently (don’t brown).
Add garlic, cook low 6–8 mins until soft.
Add sage, fry 1–2 mins until aromatic.
Add pasta water/stock gradually to form a glossy emulsion.
Add pecorino off heat, whisk smooth.
Season with pepper, lemon zest + juice.

candidates.description: This North Indian curry base draws on the rich, creamy, and aromatic traditions of Delhi-style cooking. It balances the tang of tomatoes with the mellow sweetness of coconut, deeply spiced with warm, aromatic garam masala and the bittersweet, herbal note of dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi). BASE SAUCE RECIPE (Tomato–Coconut–Spice) A luxurious cooking sauce traditionally found in Delhi Tomato Base: Chopped tomatoes and tomato paste, providing the primary tangy body. Creaminess: Coconut milk and coconut powder (often blended with creamy dairy like yogurt/buttermilk powder in Delhi-style). Aromatics: Finely chopped onions, ginger, and garlic, sautéed until caramelized. Spice Mix: A robust blend of garam masala, turmeric, chili powder (often Kashmiri for color), coriander, and cumin. Key Herb: Dried Fenugreek Leaves (Kasuri Methi), which are added towards the end to provide an earthy, bittersweet aroma characteristic of North Indian cooking. Base Oil: Often Rapeseed or Mustard oil, used to fry spices. Yield: ~50 portions service sauce
methodSteps: Sweat onions in oil until fully soft (no colour).
Add garlic + ginger; cook 2 mins.
Add spices; cook 1–2 mins.
Add tomatoes; simmer 25–35 mins until thick.
Add coconut milk; simmer 20 mins.
Blend smooth if required.
Finish with garam masala + crushed kasuri methi, adjust seasoning.

candidates.description: This recipe creates a deconstructed, bowl-style version of the iconic Kolkata Kathi Roll, focusing on a creamy, tangy yogurt-tomato-cumin base that marinades the protein and acts as a flavourful dressing. BASE SAUCE RECIPE (Yogurt–Tomato–Cumin) Yield: ~50 portions
methodSteps: Heat oil; temper mustard + cumin seeds.
Add onions; sweat until soft.
Add garlic + ginger; cook 2 mins.
Add tomatoes + spices; simmer until thick.
Reduce heat; whisk yogurt in gradually (don’t boil hard).
Simmer gently 5–10 mins. Finish with lemon + coriander.
The "Kolkata" Essentials (Freshness & Crunch)
Sliced Red Onions: Tossed with a little lemon juice, salt, and black salt.
Julienned Cucumbers : For crunch.
Green Chilies: Finely chopped.
Fresh Coriander (Dhaniya): Chopped.
Chaat Masala: A final sprinkle over the whole bowl.
TO FINISH
Add the cooked protein (paneer/chicken).
Add a generous scoop of the fresh raw onion and cucumber salad.
Drizzle more of the raw Yogurt-Tomato-Cumin sauce over the top.
Finish with fresh coriander, a squeeze of lime, and a sprinkle of chaat masala.
“Final part for the assembly - Thinly sliced raw onion, green chili depending how much heat you are ok with, a squeeze of lime and sprinkle some chat masala.”

candidates.description: This Punjabi-style base sauce (or masala) for dal and bean stews is characterized by a rich, slow-cooked foundation of sautéed onions, garlic, ginger, and tomatoes, which is combined with cooked lentils and their stock, then simmered for a creamy, concentrated flavor. BASE MASALA RECIPE (Tomato–Onion Masala) Ghee or butter (often a mix) is used to sauté aromatics, providing a rich, authentic flavor. Aromatics: Finely chopped or grated white/red onions, followed by a generous amount of ginger-garlic paste. Spices: Cumin seeds (sizzled first), Kashmiri red chili powder (for color without excessive heat), garam masala, turmeric, and dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi). Yield: ~50 portions
methodSteps: Sweat onions until soft then lightly golden.
Add garlic + ginger; cook 2 mins.
Add spices; cook out.
Add tomatoes; simmer until thick and jammy.
Add lentil stock to desired consistency; simmer.
Finish with tadka if desired (ghee + cumin + garlic + chilli).
The secret to the deep flavour is simmering for a long time, allowing the lentils to break down into the sauce.
The sauce is ready when the tomato-onion mixture releases   fat/oil, indicating the aromatics are fully cooked.

candidates.description: This South Indian Coconut-Tamarind-Tomato Curry (Kerala Style) is a fragrant, creamy, and slightly tangy coconut-based sauce, characterizing the coastal cuisine of Kerala. It is often described as a lighter, fresh alternative to northern Indian curries, featuring a vibrant blend of spices, coconut, and tamarind that creates a, harmonious balance of flavors. BASE SAUCE RECIPE (Coconut–Tamarind–Tomato) Creamy, tangy, and subtly spiced, often balanced with a hint of jaggery or sugar to offset the tartness of the tamarind. Key Ingredients: Coconut milk (or paste), tamarind extract, fresh tomatoes, mustard seeds, and curry leaves. Yield: ~50 portions
methodSteps: Temper mustard seeds + curry leaves in oil.
Add onions; sweat until soft.
Add garlic + ginger; cook 2 mins.
Add tomatoes + spices; simmer 20 mins.
Add tamarind + coconut milk; simmer gently 15 mins.
Balance seasoning (salt + a little sugar if sharp).

candidates.description: The Coastal/Bengali Fish Curry Bowl features a classic Bengali-style Mustard-Tomato-Tamarind sauce, characterized by a piquant, tangy, and slightly pungent flavor profile. This sauce is typically built on a pungent mustard oil base, thickened with tomatoes, and soured with tamarind, creating a vibrant, often thin, or medium-thick gravy designed to be served over rice. BASE SAUCE RECIPE (Mustard–Tomato–Tamarind) The sauce is initiated by heating raw mustard oil until it smokes, tempered with panch phoran (Bengali five-spice: cumin, mustard, fennel, fenugreek, and nigella seeds) or just cumin/mustard seeds. Yield: ~50 portions
methodSteps: Sweat onions until soft.
Add garlic + ginger; cook 2 mins.
Add tomatoes + turmeric + chilli; simmer 15–20 mins.
Stir in mustard paste + tamarind; simmer gently 10 mins (don’t boil hard).
Adjust seasoning.

sourceParagraphs: This vibrant Tibetan-style Thukpa bowl features a nutrient-dense, spicy vegetable broth crafted from a base of sautéed garlic, ginger, fresh tomatoes, and assorted vegetables, seasoned with turmeric, chili powder, and aromatic timur (Sichuan pepper) for a unique numbing heat. It is a comforting, healthy, high-fiber noodle soup, often enriched with soy sauce, vinegar, and fresh herbs like coriander, making it a popular winter staple.
The broth is built by stir-frying garlic, ginger, and green chilies, followed by tomatoes and a fragrant blend of turmeric, chilli powder, and often timur (Sichuan pepper) or garam masala.
Season. Strain for clean broth or keep rustic.
Finish with toasted coriander seeds + coriander cress.

candidates.description: Oaxacan Mole Bowls feature a complex, dark, and rich sauce (mole negro) made from charred chilies (such as Chilhuacle), dried fruits, nuts, spices, and dark chocolate, served over grains and vegetables. This traditional, labour-intensive sauce is known for its sweet, Savory, and spicy flavour profile, commonly served over chicken or in plant-based Buddha bowls. BASE SAUCE – Dark Mole (Chilli–Fruit–Chocolate) (Weights for 50) The process requires toasting ingredients until deeply browned (or slightly burnt      for the "Negro" colour), blending with broth (or water for vegan) and dark chocolate, then simmering to thicken.
methodSteps: Toast dried chillies quickly (do not burn), soak in hot water 20 mins. Roast onions/garlic hard for colour. Blend chillies with tomatoes, raisins, nuts/seeds, spices, tortillas/breadcrumb. Cook paste in oil 20 mins, stirring. Add stock and simmer 45–60 mins. Blend smooth. Finish with chocolate, adjust salt/sugar.

Sesame paste (Chinese sesame paste or tahini): 1.2kg
Warm chilli oil gently. Fry garlic + ginger 1 min.
Add soy, vinegar, sugar, stock and simmer 10 mins.
Whisk sesame paste with hot stock until smooth, then add back in.
Keep hot and whisk before service (sesame separates).
Additional Aromatics: Often enhanced with soy sauce, black vinegar, Sichuan peppercorn powder (for numbing), and sometimes sesame paste or peanut butter for body.

candidates.description: Chongqing-style hot pot bowls feature a, intensely spicy and numbing broth, known for its deep red, oil-rich base made from Sichuan chili peppers, Sichuan peppercorns, broad bean paste (doubanjiang), garlic, ginger, and fermented black beans BASE SAUCE – Spicy Hot Pot Broth – 50 portions This aromatic, flavourful soup is typically created by simmering these spices in beef tallow or vegetable oil and combining with chicken or vegetable broth.
methodSteps: Heat oil. Fry garlic/ginger.
Add doubanjiang + hot pot paste, fry 6–8 mins until red oil.
Add spices + chillies, fry 1–2 mins.
Add soy, wine, stock, sugar. Simmer 45 mins.
Strain if needed (or keep rustic).

candidates.description: Chengdu Mapo Bowls feature a rich, numbing-and-spicy (mala) sauce based on Pixian fermented chili bean paste (doubanjiang) and Sichuan pepper, fry the paste in oil to develop deep red colour and Savory flavour. The braise is built with aromatics like ginger, garlic, and scallions, often using beef broth and soy sauce to coat tofu and minced meat. BASE SAUCE – Mapo Braise (Pixian + Sichuan Pepper) – 50 portions The sauce is designed to be deeply savory, with a bright red color from the oil and a strong, aromatic finish.
methodSteps: Heat oil. Fry garlic, ginger, spring onion whites 1–2 mins.
Add Pixian paste and fry 5–7 mins until the oil turns red (key step).
Add soy, wine, stock, sugar,  Simmer 20 mins.
Thicken with slurry to sauce consistency.
Finish with Sichuan pepper + sesame oil.

candidates.description: Mianyang-style Chilli Tomato Braised Bowls are a Savory, umami-rich dish featuring noodles or protein braised in a robust sauce of fresh tomatoes, aromatic chilli oil, and soy sauce BASE SAUCE – Tomato + Chilli + Soy– 50 portions This Sichuan-influenced, "red-cooked" (hongshao) style balances heat and acidity, creating a thick sauce meant for coating noodles or stewing meats like beef shank. Base Sauce: A mixture of sautéed, crushed tomatoes for sweetness, chilli oil (or fresh chillies) for heat, and soy sauce (light and dark) for saltiness and colour. Aromatics: Typically includes garlic, ginger, green onions, and sometimes star anise or cinnamon.
methodSteps: Sweat onions. Add garlic/ginger.
Add chilli paste and cook out 2 mins.
Add tomatoes + purée, then soy, sugar, wine, stock.
Simmer 60 mins
Optional: thicken lightly with slurry.

candidates.description: Based on the ingredients listed, Chengdu Sweet & Sour Bowls feature a bold, Savory-tangy profile that combines the sweetness of tomato, the deep acidity of fermented black vinegar (often Chinkiang vinegar), and the heat of chilli. BASE SAUCE – Tomato + Black Vinegar + Chilli – 50 portions Tomato: Tomato paste or ketchup, which provides body and a Savory-sweet base.
